title: We Have Heard the Wondrous Story
description: We Have Heard the Wondrous Story in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns of the Greek Church (Edinburgh and London, 1900).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: We have heard the won-drous sto-ry Of the Re-sur-rec-tion morn; We have seen its match-less glo-ry, Christ the ri-sen Lord a-dorn.

lines: We have heard the wondrous story
We have seen its matchless glory,
Men with erring sinners found Thee,
And upon a Cross they bound Thee,
For the good that Thou hadst done;
We have heard the wondrous story
Christ our God, to Him be glory,
For He casts death's bands away.
Come, ye faithful, come with gladness,
For the Cross was shorn of sadness

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Greek Church (1900)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Greek Church; set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
